message.reasoning:
I need to respond to a Monopoly trade offer.

The counter-trade offers Pacific Avenue for Ventnor Avenue plus $50. I own Pacific and have cash, but the opponent holds North Carolina and Pennsylvania.

This is a color-group-for-color-group swap. Pacific would complete the opponent's green monopoly, which is far more valuable than my yellow one. They could build on it once they unmortgage Pennsylvania.

I will reject the offer. Pacific is too valuable to give away, and the $50 cash would help them survive. I am now looking for a counter-offer that keeps Pacific but still gets Ventnor.

I cannot build the yellow monopoly with only $221. The dark blue group already has one house each, and upgrading it to two houses each costs $400. My prior plan was to mortgage Atlantic, Marvin, and Pacific for roughly $420, add my current cash, build the dark blues, and keep about $241.

A yellow monopoly without cash to build is weaker than the two-house dark blue group. Ventnor alone is not worth the trade. I cannot counter with more cash because I only have $221.

A cash-only counter would waste my remaining money and let them survive my Boardwalk. I will reject the offer outright. I will send a brief public message that declines without revealing my full strategy.

I am drafting a public message that Pacific stays and the opponent must name a cash-only offer for Ventnor. I will formalize this as a counter-trade rather than a simple rejection.

I will reject the offer outright. A counter with more cash or Atlantic would waste my money or break my yellow set. Pacific is too valuable to give away.
